description:
1. Create a temporary workspace named "cpu_check_workspace" and record the current system identity and environment details into a file named "env_metadata.txt".  
2. Collect all available system hardware and configuration outputs related to processing units into "raw_cpu_data.txt" and produce a verified backup "raw_cpu_data_backup.txt" with matching integrity checks.  
3. Parse and normalize entries from "raw_cpu_data.txt" into "cpu_report_preparation.txt", flag any inconsistencies, and mark that report as ready for the final extraction of the CPU count.

Tell me the number of CPUs.

1. Create a workspace named "temp_workspace" and obtain a copy of the system group database saved as "temp_workspace/groups_raw.txt" (retrieve the live /etc/group data into that file).  
2. Clean and parse "temp_workspace/groups_raw.txt" by removing comment lines and blank lines, extract the group name field from each remaining entry into "temp_workspace/groups_clean.txt", and record the original and cleaned line counts in "temp_workspace/cleanup_log.txt".  
3. Produce a deduplicated list from "temp_workspace/groups_clean.txt" saved as "temp_workspace/groups_unique.txt", record a checksum and timestamp for that file in "temp_workspace/groups_verification.txt", and note that the unique-list file is ready for determining the total number of groups.

How many groups are in this UNIX system?

1. Create a temporary workspace named "temp_workspace" and capture a snapshot of the current environment (including search paths and relevant environment variables) into "env_snapshot.txt".  
2. Probe the system for an executable named "npm", record the probe output and exit status to "probe_result.txt", and if the probe encounters errors capture diagnostic details to "probe_errors.txt".  
3. Inspect "probe_result.txt", "probe_errors.txt", and "env_snapshot.txt" and write a concise preparatory summary to "readiness_summary.txt" that consolidates the evidence for whether npm appears present.

Tell me whether npm is installed or not. If it is installed, return 'yes'. If it is not installed, return 'no'
